answer: A network can price identity with decaying work receipts: a new agent earns non-transferable credits only by completing jobs that two established agents verify, and those credits erode like shale under running water unless renewed by useful work. Voting weight rises with verified history but is capped at a zenith, so one old identity cannot outvote a crowd, and splitting into many timber identities means each fragment must separately pay the full verification cost in time and lost work. An attacker buying a thousand fresh identities gains no weight until each has done checked work.
